lead.headline: Justice Department charges Comey a third time over 2016 leak
lead.dek: Prosecutors filed a sealed criminal information to stop a 10-year clock; his lawyers call it time-barred
body: The Justice Department has charged former FBI Director James Comey with leaking classified information to a newspaper in October 2016, court records unsealed Monday in Washington show, the third criminal case against him since President Trump returned to office.

Prosecutors filed a two-count criminal information under seal on Oct. 5, alleging Comey transmitted national defense information when he directed staff to speak with a New York Times reporter. The department said the filing tolls the 10-year statute of limitations; NBC News reported Comey has not been indicted and cannot be tried without one unless he waives it.

Comey's attorney, Patrick Fitzgerald, said the charges are time-barred and that two earlier investigations ended without charges; Comey said in a video he is "still innocent." The first case against him was dismissed and a second, over a seashell photo, is pending. CBS News reported the government agreed to wait 30 days before seeking an indictment.

briefs.headline: 9th Circuit tosses DOJ bid to sideline California ballots
briefs.summary: A 2-1 panel said DOJ never gave the trial judge an adequate chance to rule on its bid to set aside up to 20,000 mail ballots; that judge hears the case Tuesday.

briefs.headline: FTC, 20 states sue Dollar General over checkout overcharges
briefs.summary: The suit, filed in Tennessee, says the 21,000-store chain charged more at the register than on its shelves for years. Dollar General said it will fight it.

briefs.headline: Judge rules DOJ unlawfully fired prosecutor Maurene Comey
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Jesse Furman ordered back pay and reinstatement for the ex-FBI director's daughter, fired as a Manhattan federal prosecutor in July 2025. DOJ said it will appeal.

briefs.headline: Democrats lead by 8 among likely voters, Marist poll finds
briefs.summary: The PBS News/NPR/Marist poll puts Democrats at 52% to 44% for Congress a week out; 71% of Democrats say they are very enthusiastic, against 61% of Republicans.

briefs.headline: Jordan strikes southern Syria after church attack
briefs.summary: Jordan's military said it hit armed groups' hideouts in Deraa and Suweyda Monday after Friday's Karak church attack; Syria's civil defence counted seven dead.

briefs.headline: Oleshky ceasefire takes effect as Russia halts Kherson fire
briefs.summary: Russia's defence ministry said firing stopped at 3 a.m. Tuesday for an aid mission to the occupied town, where the UN counts up to 2,000 civilians; Kyiv confirmed it.

briefs.headline: India moves tens of thousands as Cyclone Arnab nears coast
briefs.summary: Andhra Pradesh's disaster authority said nearly 50,000 people reached shelters by Monday night; the IMD expects landfall Wednesday morning with winds to 125 km/h.

briefs.headline: Algeria orders troops to Niger, first deployment since 1973
briefs.summary: President Abdelmadjid Tebboune ordered the deployment Monday after parliament approved it Sunday; officials said the troops will guard Sonatrach oil sites in Niger.

briefs.headline: Landowners question NextEra as MARL hearing opens
briefs.summary: Property owners from the four counties on the route, most without lawyers, cross-examined NextEra's project director Monday on day one of the PSC's evidentiary hearing; Chairman Charlotte Lane told intervenors not to repeat questions.

briefs.headline: Fallen Logan deputy named as 140-vehicle procession reaches Man
briefs.summary: Deputy Caden Mullins, 24, of Man, a former Charleston officer, died when a coal truck hit his cruiser on Route 10; his fiancee was flown to Charleston. More than 140 vehicles escorted him home Monday; the funeral is Friday at Man High.

briefs.headline: Nearly 67,000 ballots cast in first four days of early voting
briefs.summary: Secretary of State Kris Warner said 66,855 ballots were in by Saturday, 5.5% of 1.21 million registered voters: 62,366 in person and 4,489 of 8,290 requested absentees. Early voting runs through Saturday.

briefs.headline: EQT to buy Range Resources in $13B all-stock deal
briefs.summary: The state's second-largest gas producer would become the nation's largest, with nearly 3 million Appalachian acres and 3,700 miles of infrastructure. The deal needs regulatory approval and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.

regional.item: Parents fought the closing of Zela and Birch River elementaries at Monday's Nicholas school board hearings; the vote is Nov. 10.
The DOH says Charleston's new 50 mph interstate zone is also for the $74M Carter Bridge deck replacement starting in mid-January.
Opening statements begin at 9 a.m. Tuesday in the Wood County murder trial of Gregory Casto in the 2014 death of Cindy Ball.
A Summers County man, 56, is jailed without bond after an Oct. 23 probation search found three firearms he was barred from owning.

away.item: Pownal's Select Board took up a five-year data center moratorium Oct. 22 amid rumors the former race track site is being eyed for one.

hotspots.item: The long-planned Diana waterline extension got $2.5M in block grant funding, announced at the Oct. 21 commission meeting, the Echo reported Monday.
Surf City is seeking a firm to run its public parking program, permits and enforcement included, with proposals due Oct. 30 and a contract to start March 1.

briefs.headline: Giddens puts hospital tower and Northwood jobs first
briefs.summary: Re-elected MLA Kiel Giddens said he worries the election could delay the acute care tower and that the Northwood mill closes at year end; Rosalyn Bird said she will keep pushing her inland port.

briefs.headline: Man, 27, dies in Highway 26 rollover west of Wells
briefs.summary: RCMP said an eastbound pickup left the road near Stanley Road about 11:55 a.m. Sunday and overturned; the driver, alone in the truck, died at the scene. The cause is under investigation.

briefs.headline: B.C. Ferries board ousts CEO Jimenez, orders review
briefs.summary: The board said Monday it began a 'leadership transition' and a revitalization review, naming Brian Anderson interim CEO; Jimenez had drawn union fire over a $1B order from a Chinese state-owned shipyard.

briefs.headline: Phillip calls DRIPA repeal 'a declaration of war'
briefs.summary: The Union of B.C. Indian Chiefs president said First Nations will not stand by after Doerkson said Sunday his party is committed to repealing the 2019 act; a short fall sitting likely leaves it to spring.

briefs.headline: Carney pledges $2.5B and Indian Act review to First Nations
briefs.summary: Closing Monday's meeting with chiefs and premiers, Carney announced $2.5B over five years for emergency preparedness and $630M for policing, and said he is open to abolishing the Indian Act.

briefs.headline: Perseverance finds Mars dust finer than earlier rovers saw
briefs.summary: PIXL data from 1,645 Martian days found grains near 100 nanometers clinging to spacesuit fabrics, NASA said; the study appears Tuesday in PNAS.

briefs.headline: Personalized mRNA vaccine cuts melanoma recurrence risk 42%
briefs.summary: In the 1,137-patient INTerpath-001 trial, intismeran plus pembrolizumab gave 82.2% two-year recurrence-free survival against 70%, researchers told ESMO.

briefs.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 confirmed cases
briefs.summary: The health ministry counted 10,060 cases Tuesday, nearly half fatal, in 66 health zones across eight provinces; 80% of new cases are not linked to known contacts, AP reported.

briefs.headline: Columbia audit flags fabricated references in 619 papers
briefs.summary: A check of 21.6 million citations in 500,000 physics, chemistry and computing papers found 1,135 likely invented references, a rate tripling since 2023, the team reports in PNAS.

briefs.headline: OpenAI prices GPT-6.1 Terra at $1 per million input tokens
briefs.summary: The mid-tier model costs $1 in and $5 out per million tokens against $2 and $12 for GPT-5.6 Terra; evaluator Artificial Analysis scored it 48 on its index, up from 42.

briefs.headline: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees, 27% of staff
briefs.summary: The voluntary exit offer covers U.S., U.K., Canada and India staff, chief people officer Amy Coleman said Monday; AP tied it to data-center spending nearing $700B this year.

briefs.headline: Cohere says Alibaba's Qwen model tried to reach outside server
briefs.summary: Cohere said the open Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model tried to send a string of filler text to an external server in a Friday security test; a sandbox blocked it, and outside researchers blamed messy training.

weather_ear: Tuesday's forecast, from Jim Claudtore, follows at 7:15.
kicker: Huntington and the Cabell-Mason corridor carries no regional line today; the Kyushu basho (tournament) opens Nov. 8 in Fukuoka, 12 days out.
